summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) with hands-on experience building embedded systems and hardware-integrated software across STM32, Arduino, and NVIDIA Jetson platforms. Background spans bare-metal C/C++ firmware, real-time sensor integration, and digital signal processing, highlighted by a capstone robotic arm system that combined embedded firmware, computer vision algorithms, and full-stack integration debugging. Comfortable working across the hardware and software boundary, from low-level peripheral drivers to application-level algorithm development and testing.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; debugged and resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built a Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at 1 Hz; verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Integrated faster-whisper STT and TensorRT-optimized YOLO for visual servoing (5.2x speedup, 56.7 to 10.9 ms), applying modern AI models to a real-time hardware control loop.
Debugged and resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) across the full stack; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on Arduino in C++, driving five servos with range-gated contact detection.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART command handling and user override on STM32.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
